motion.name: stamp-press
motion.purpose: The single motion moment: stamp impressions land at scale(1.18)->1 with opacity 0->1 (complete by 60%), settling at the stamp's -4deg rest angle. Keyframes: from { transform: rotate(-4deg) scale(1.18); opacity: 0 } 60% { opacity: 1 } to { transform: rotate(-4deg) scale(1); opacity: 1 }. Fires only when an impression is actually laid down. Disabled under prefers-reduced-motion (animation: none; scroll-behavior: auto) — stamps still appear; evidence must not depend on motion.

motion.name: scroll-glide
motion.purpose: Root smooth scrolling for in-page anchors; reverts to auto under prefers-reduced-motion.

a11y.stateEncoding: State is always mark + rule form + text (✓/✕/·, struck line-through, 3px double rule, -4deg stamp, inverted fill); hue only reinforces. Color-blind safe by construction.
a11y.focusVisible: 2px solid #33506e outline, 2px offset, on every interactive element; queue rows and tabs keyboard-reachable (WCAG 2.1.1).
a11y.contrastFloors: ink/bone 13.8:1 · ink/pink 11.4:1 · ink/green 12.4:1 · stamp-ink/pink 5.9:1 · pen/bone 7.3:1 · ink-70-on-bone 5.9:1 · stamp/bone 5.2:1 — all AA or better at their sizes.
a11y.reducedMotion: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce disables the stamp press and smooth scrolling; stamps appear instantly.

narrative.overview:
The console is one continuous carbon-copy docket. Every write is a docketed triplicate — the send gate, the audit anchor and the encrypted backup are the three copies you can see — and the interface refuses the category's three-pane mail client and the card-dashboard rut outright. The world is NCR carbonless business-form printing, 1950s–70s: bone / pale-pink / pale-green stock under process ink, rubber-stamp vermilion for dispositions, ballpoint blue for human sign-off. The page reads as one form you work down: docket header band, perforated stub rail, ruled working boxes, stamp strip, sign-off margin. The memorable moment is the triplicate press: a confirmed action visibly stamps its three copies — GATE, AUDIT, BACKUP — so evidence is seen, not promised.

Provenance: roll assignment from seed key 8345aab6, grounded candidate 7 of 7, user-confirmed as "Carbon Copy Docket — THE ROLL"; the approved sketch is .impeccable/mocks/decision/assigned.html and the decision round is recorded in .impeccable/mocks/decision/payload.json. Two named raises were carried into the build and are invariants of this system: from the Design Annual challenger, every confirmed send carries a human sign-off mark in the margin — the machine never signs for you; from the Grid Specimen challenger, the construction grid stays visible as hairline ruling in empty ground — the machine shows its work.

Honesty is the personality, per PRODUCT.md's brand commitments: unverified things are never shown green, states say "not_configured" rather than faking health, and stamps fire only on actual command outcomes. Two API-driven substitutions (recorded as amendments in the surface brief on 2026-11-01) keep the docket honest: the header carries only fields the live routes expose — docket id · revision, gate posture (sending_enabled × mode), last poll — with no "send cap", "confidence" or model-identity cells, and no phantom gmail_send_scope signal.
keyCharacteristics: One continuous form: ruled boxes with inverted ink corner labels, never cards.
Triplicate logic everywhere: three stock tints map to GATE / AUDIT / BACKUP.
State is a stamp mark (✓ ✕ ·, struck line, double rule, rotated VOID) — hue only reinforces.
Form-printed type: tracked Archivo small caps as printed labels, Courier Prime as typed values.
Flat, square, hairline-ruled: zero border-radius, zero shadows; the construction grid shows in empty ground.
One motion moment only: the stamp press.

rules.name: The Hue-Never-Alone Rule
rules.body: Hue never carries state alone. Every state is a stamp mark first — a glyph (✓ ✕ ·), a struck line-through, a double rule, a rotated band, an inverted fill — and the tint only reinforces it. Removing all color must leave every state readable.

rules.name: The Honest Green Rule
rules.body: Pale green means exactly two things: third copy, or a verified pass. Nothing is green until a real outcome says so — unconfigured states print "not_configured", never a friendly tint.

rules.name: The Three-Copy Rule
rules.body: Bone / pink / green always read as copy 1 GATE / 2 AUDIT / 3 BACKUP in that order (the header legend and the impression strip both spell it out). Do not reuse the tints in a new meaning without a spelled-out legend.

rules.name: The Printed-vs-Typed Rule
rules.body: Structure is printed (Archivo tracked caps); content is typed (Courier Prime). A value never appears in Archivo and a label never appears in Courier. code tokens get a pink ground to stay visibly typed.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Anything numeric that can change — countdowns, impression timestamps — uses tabular numerals (font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums) so the type doesn't jitter as values tick.

rules.name: The One-Docket Rule
rules.body: The whole console is one form. Regions are boxes with corner labels or hairline-divided cells — never floating cards, never nested panels.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Depth comes from tint and rule weight only. Adding a shadow or a radius imports a different world.

rules.name: The Hairline Grid Rule
rules.body: Empty ground always shows the construction grid at grid-faint strength (and the reply editor carries the same ruling at one-axis pitch). It is the honesty of the medium — the grid the form was printed on.

rules.name: The Stamp Angle Rule
rules.body: Rotation is a stamp privilege. Nothing else in the system is ever rotated.

rules.name: The Machine-Never-Signs Rule
rules.body: Human sign-off is a blank margin in ballpoint blue. The interface may ask for a signature; it never produces one.

rules.name: The Outcome-Stamped Rule
rules.body: Stamps reflect actual command outcomes only. A filed (non-send) write stamps copies 2 and 3 — AUDIT and BACKUP — and leaves the GATE copy bare, because no send happened. A refused send strikes the GATE copy '— VOID', marks layers 2 and 3 with struck ✕ and raises the VOID stamp. A completed send stamps all three copies with ✓ + time and marks all three layers ✓. Nothing is pre-stamped, estimated, or stamped in anticipation.

dos: Do carry every state as a mark plus a rule form plus text — ✓/✕/· glyphs, struck lines, double rules, inverted fills — and let the tint only reinforce it (the Hue-Never-Alone Rule).
Do print structure in tracked Archivo caps and type values in Courier Prime with tabular numerals (the Printed-vs-Typed Rule).
Do keep the construction grid visible at grid-faint (24px pitch) in empty ground and the editor (the Hairline Grid Rule).

Do show only fields the live API actually exposes in docketed header/record cells — the amendments to the surface brief exist precisely for this; unverified state prints its real word ("not_configured"), never a friendly tint.
Do give every interactive element the 2px pen :focus-visible ring at 2px offset, and keep queue rows and tabs keyboard-reachable (WCAG 2.1.1).
Do stamp impressions only after the command resolves (the Outcome-Stamped Rule).
donts: Don't use hue alone for state, and don't use pale green for anything unverified (the Honest Green Rule).
Don't add border-radius (0px is the system) or shadows (the No-Shadow Rule).
Don't add motion beyond the stamp press; under reduced motion, don't substitute a different flourish.
Don't rotate anything but stamps, or double-rule anything but the VOID mark (the Stamp Angle Rule).
Don't decorate with stamps, perforations or triplicate legends: the risk of this world is bureaucratic costume — the stamps stay marks of control, never clutter.
Don't build three-pane mail-client layouts or card dashboards; regions are ruled boxes with corner labels (the One-Docket Rule).
Don't mix the two type voices inside a phrase, or render a value in Archivo / a label in Courier.
